- Function values: `FunctionNode`: `Primitive | System | Defined | LateBound | Applied { op: Operator, operands } | Train(tines) | Array`; `Operator`: `Kind(OperatorKind)` | a dfn operator's closure; `FunctionData { node, environment, rules: Option<Rules> }`; `OperatorKind::info()`: call, spelling, inverse, `discards`, Python name. Internal kinds: `Framed { axes, atoms }`, `JvpStep { packing }`, `VjpStep { direction }`. The one generic binding recipe lives in `eval.rs` and is reused by `Program`. Its canonical `FunctionOperand::{Value { value, literal }, Input { position, literal }}` distinguishes real values from input positions and retains literal provenance without fake placeholder values. One `OperandKind` rule classifies structural operands, ranks included, versus data. One `Function::captured()` order covers every free datum (stored, host, pending or carried), bound data operands and array tines; capture traversal, environment binding and rebuilding use it. Cached templates contain structure and positions, never raw data, live closures or producers. Ordinary calls resolve existing Origin/frame bindings without rebuilding frozen functions; actual function results rebuild from the run's values. There is no separate template IR, registry, `FunctionView` or replay-time `free_value` lookup (parts 10, 19).
- Cache: `Programs::serve(base, current_origin)` checks discovered-read guards in the one function-structure store. One cached `Recording` holds the program, logical output description, effects, itemwise/error properties and discovered reads for ordinary invocation, case planning and loops. A dfn keys by a weak reference to its `Definition`, never a closure instance. A forced graph uses its structure key; unowned entries are evicted least recently used past 256. `Key` uses per-axis 0/1/more length classes, axis equalities and the other description, structural and parameter facts in part 10. All call-time captured-data inputs follow part 10; there is no stored/host free-facts comparison or late session reread. Each plan keeps the leaf range boxes it assumes.
- Refill: `Plan::refill(from, running)` derives descriptions and maps through origins and their row-plan builders, starting at 0 or after a data-determined length. The same bound inputs and prefix values supply parameters and callable bindings through the borrowed call view. A replay and a cached graph read use it when lengths or count parameters changed. It never gathers, rewrites, orders or places stage ends. Refill validates the plan's kind, range and structural assumptions before execution under the existing guard/miss policy. Run preparation then selects part 8's count-dependent choices, including on-demand compilation.
- Loop: `Step::Loop` has a bound body/template, exit, carry and noncarry/captured input positions; rules `batched`, `jvp`, `transposed`, `substituted` (the inverse rule: a negative count or `¯∞` loops over `f⁻¹`, `Applied(Inverse, f)`, at the positive count): `batched`, `jvp` and `substituted` return the rebuilt `Origin<Vec<Value>>` for the loop whose body is `Applied(kind, f)`; reverse linearization splits before building executable loops (part 15); `transposed` builds the normal reverse loop over the separate linear body. Bound forward JVPs may keep joint outputs. Packing covers carry, noncarry and captured leaves relative to the current level. Every transformed call preserves mode, literal marks, argument trees, explicit-boundary metadata, settings and capture bindings through the origin projection; no helper returns a bare operation/list or reloads session preferences.
- Errors: rustymath owns the first-error slot and count held by `Session::error`; `Session::raise() -> Result<()>` raises at checkpoints. Checking follows the call's origin (Measures). Runners compare counts around steps; no error restarts a read. Static graph-numeric steps remain memory-safe without recording data errors.
- Effects: `Step::Effect` takes the previous effect's token and its operands. Outside a recording it runs at its call. No session registry. Settings belong to origins (part 4).
- Writes: `selection::selecting(target, root) -> Result<Option<Walk>>`: a walk writes through one `At` node; a computing target uses its inverse; an invalid selection raises.

## Numerical algorithms

General positive floating Pow/Root composes the shared Exp/Ln formulas: `exp(y*ln(x))` and `exp(ln(x)/n)`. Preserve cheap constant/integer powers, sqrt/Cbrt, exact arithmetic and zero/negative/parity/domain semantics. Remove general Pow's table/compensation machinery. Characterize float errors and document function-specific exceptions without weakening common-use results or exact arithmetic. Accuracy characterization uses `u*|y ln(x)|` (unit roundoff u) for Pow, not the exponent alone; f32 and f64 need their own bounds.

Trig keeps short fast reduction and polynomials. Rare out-of-range lanes use the object's scalar platform/native sin/cos/tan repair instead of porting custom Payne–Hanek u128/table arithmetic into Ops. The predicate and its limits have one home (part 6); range-proof elimination belongs to part 2, compiled repair ordering to part 9. Native/wasm provider and ABI selection must preserve the semantic and speed requirements. GPU execution needs device code or portable lowering, not necessarily another mathematical implementation.

Reuse rustymath's existing optimized elementwise, reduction and contraction drivers through shared interfaces co-designed with BPL. Keep repair and error reporting outside their common hot loops. Do not add new SIMD code or a separate vector execution engine in the foundation-writing and integration stages. Once the foundation works, measure before changing performance code. Preserve non-FMA f32 trig's f64 intermediates through the existing width operations. A retained algorithm that needs table lookup can use the existing scalar loads or platform operations.

Keep Cbrt's compact fixed algorithm: two f32 or three f64 Newton steps and correction. Incomplete Gamma/Beta convergence computes the answer and stays in canonical object-backed Calls where appropriate. Ordinary Gamma/Beta do not require those convergence loops. Substantial algorithms need neither a general numerical-loop IR nor a blanket vector-call ABI. Host exact arithmetic and native f16/complex retain the coverage in parts 1, 6 and 9; block admission does not decide correctness coverage.

Shared formulas and object-backed Calls must each have one mathematical implementation. An algorithm's call/staging and lost-fusion costs belong to the normal speed budgets, not an assumed fixed one- or two-copy charge. Preserve the documented finite-result bounds until characterized exceptions are documented. Performance and simplicity outrank accuracy machinery beyond those requirements.

## Cost model

What each stage of the pipeline ought to cost, counted from the work it must do and set beside the role models. Never from today's tree: a stage over its budget is a gap in that stage's code. Estimates cover a single-output call with at most 2 operands; cost variable operands, output descriptions and argument trees at their actual sizes. Units: instructions retired (`instructions`, Apple silicon) per call, node, step or run; work per item in copies (DEV.md).

### Primitive operations

Assumed, Rust on Apple silicon, small sizes:
- small allocation (size-classed allocator) 40; free 30; `Arc` clone or drop 5
- hash of a small key (≤32 B) 15; map probe, hit 40; insert 60
- indirect call 10
- a `Desc` (kind, atom flag, layout of rank ≤4, range) 30; a kind, shape or range rule 40-100 (2 operands' agreement at the top)
- a `Mapping` built or composed 30-60
- work per item: elementwise f64 0.5-1 (2-lane NEON, unrolled); copy 0.5; fold 1

### Stage budgets

| Stage | Work it must do | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| dispatch, 1 call | innermost level among ≤2 args (10); row by index (5); roles (10); captured input binding (20 a captured leaf); kind, shape, range and validity rules (100); node allocated and filled (70); interned: hash, probe (60) | 300 + 20·captured leaves |
| pending node | node and origin: about 150 B for a single-output call, plus variable operand references, output descriptions and argument trees; leaves stay alive, no intermediate is stored | 0 |
| read of a pending graph of N nodes, plan cached | structure key: each node's step and operand descriptions hashed (30 a node); probe (40); per step: executor call (15), output allocation (40), kernel setup including cheap actual-count choices (50), work; each intermediate freed at its last use (30); `Live::of`'s walk (20 a node) and allocation (50); leaves bound to the plan's inputs (20 a leaf); the intern table updated as each node is replaced by its result or dies (30 a node) | 150 + 235·N + work |
| plan, a cache miss | `Program::of` and gather (30 a node); rewrite: root-key probe (20 a node), match and build (200 a rule applied); order (20 a node); stage ends (20 a node); descriptions and maps (130 a node); plan allocated (50 a node) | 270·N + 200·rules |
| refill | descriptions and maps at the run's lengths through the plan's own builders (130 a node); no gather, rewrite, order, stage ends or compile decision | 130·N, only where lengths or count parameters differ from the plan's last refill |
| trace | the run's own dispatch and reads, plus input roles and the key (30 an input); capture binding was paid at dispatch | dispatch + 50 a call |
| replay | key: all input descriptions hashed (30 each), inputs bound (20 each), boxes checked; probe (40); refill where lengths or count parameters changed; run as a read (135 a step + work) | 150 + 135·N + refill + work |
| compile (JIT) | only the selected useful version where its formula repays (part 9); code owned by `jit::KERNELS`, keyed by emitted structure, types and modes, never by counts | per formula |
| tree op, dfn call | op 30; name load 10; dfn frame 60 + 20 an argument | — |

Base budgets assume at most two input leaves and no additional captured data; extra leaves incur the binding/hash work listed in each row. Role models for the shape of these costs: JAX's eager mode runs each primitive as a 1-op compiled program cached by primitive and abstract signature (`apply_primitive`); `jit` checks a cache keyed by the function and its arguments' signatures, so a hit costs a key check plus the program. tinygrad builds every op as a lazy `UOp`, caches compiled kernels by their AST, and TinyJit replays the kernels a real run captured. BPL's budgets sit below both: no Python, no device launch before the GPU stage.

### What follows

1. Small calls: a call then a read of its result ≈ 300 + 150 + 235 = 685 + work. Every pending value keeps its node; a call matching no rule pays 1 root-key probe (20).
2. Ordinary code against replay, a body of N calls run again at the same shapes: ordinary ≈ 300·N (dispatch) + 150 + 235·N (read, plan cached by structure) = 535·N + 150; replay ≈ 150 + 135·N. About 4× at tiny sizes; at 10⁶ floats a step's work (about 10⁶) dwarfs both.
3. Lengths: per-axis 0/1/more classes, with refill when lengths or count parameters change (part 10).
   - Run preparation uses actual counts for compilation, contraction's cheaper read and recomputation when multiplicity matters. These cheap checks belong to kernel setup, outside item loops. The cached structural plan and code cache do not change for a new length alone.
   - A growing carry (1 item more each step) reuses its plan within a length class and the plan's guards. Refill plus replay is ≈ (130 + 135)·N = 265·N a step, including kernel setup. Scheduling every exact shape would cost ≈ (270 + 135)·N = 405·N a step. Geometric buffer capacity growth is independent of this key policy.
   - Refill derives descriptions and maps without structural scheduling. Run preparation uses the run's actual work estimates under normal speed budgets.
4. 1 cache, keyed by structure (part 10): a function value's entry holds its recordings; a forced graph's plan sits under its graph's structure, inputs keyed by part 10's read kinds; a lone node is a graph of 1. Ordinary code refills as a replay does: a growing value read outside a trace ≈ 300·N + 150 + (235 + 130)·N ≈ 665·N a step.
5. Memory between reads: pending graphs keep leaves alive, not intermediates. Node estimates include origins and variable operands, output descriptions and argument trees. The memory limit reads bytes from descriptions, not a call plan.
6. Scalar runs: a `⍣` loop of scalar ops is a loop node replaying its body (150 + 135·N an iteration); a scalar op outside a loop ≈ 685 (accepted: "The bar", "No cost when unused").
7. A new length alone does not produce a compiled version. Counts are run-time parameters. A useful recipe that emits different code compiles on its first justified use, then reuses that code (part 9).

### Checking

The closing pass counts each stage's functions (`call_profile`; `profile` with `defer=`) against these budgets. Over budget → a gap in that stage, fixed toward its budget, never by a 2nd route.

## The bar

Futhark, Dex and Julia set the standard. A design at least as good would meet the criteria below. Each one can be checked with `basedpl.bpltests.time_cases` or a reference test.

| Criterion | Meaning | Reference point |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient cost | The gradient of a scalar function of n variables costs a small constant multiple of one evaluation, whatever n is. | On ADBench, Futhark's full Jacobian costs 3.2 to 13.0 times the objective, and hand-written code 4.4 to 8.6 times (`links/arXiv-2202.10297.md`, section 7.1). |
| Primal cost | Under `∂`, the function's own computation runs on the same whole-array kernels as without `∂`, and keeps the fusion it would get without `∂`. The derivative adds whole-array work beside it. Nothing sends the original computation down a per-item path. | Futhark's reverse mode re-executes the original statements unchanged (`links/arXiv-2202.10297.md`, section 4). |
| Bulk preserved | The derivative of a whole-array operation is a whole-array operation. A map's derivative is a map. The transpose of indexing is an accumulation, not a one-hot array or a sequential loop. | Dex paper, sections 5.3 and 7.3. Futhark's `vjpMap`, `diffReduce` and `diffScan`. |
| Coverage | Primitives in a documented subset, trains, operators with any operand, branches through Agenda (`⍚`), and records of parameters. Recursion is out of scope (part 10). | JAX branches on traced values only through `lax.cond`, `lax.switch` and `select`. |
| One rule set | Each scalar glyph's partial derivatives are written once and serve both modes. Each linear operation has one transpose. A user rule attaches once and works in both modes. | Futhark's `Derivatives.hs`, Dex's `linearizeOp`, JAX's `custom_jvp`. |
| Higher orders | `∂∂` is `∂` applied to the function `f∂`, with no confusion between nesting levels. | ForwardDiff's tags. JAX nests transformations. |
| No cost when unused | Code that isn't differentiated runs as fast as now, except agreed exceptions. Agreed: always-lazy evaluation gives every call a node and a read, so a lone primitive call costs about 1.5 to 2 times today's eager call (about 685 instructions plus its work: "Cost model"), while dfn calls, loops and scalar recursion cost less. | |
| Errors | Construction and host errors stay checked; dynamic graph-numeric execution also checks data errors, while static graph-numeric execution follows Measures' non-raising policy. When and how a checked deferred error surfaces isn't promised. Leaving an error guard forces the work made inside it, so the guard catches its errors. Effects keep their order among themselves; an effect forces only what it reads. | `meta/ideas.md`, "Block fusion", names late errors as a cost of lazy arrays. |
| Composes with optimisation | The rewrite rules and the scheduler apply to tangent and transpose nodes as to any other nodes. Derivative code fuses, windows and stencils included. The scheduler recomputes a residual that is cheap to compute again, rather than storing it. | XLA simplifies and fuses the programs that JAX's transforms produce. |
| Evaluator | The change doesn't repeat evaluator semantics. | |
| Build time | After a small edit to one function, the dev build rebuilds about as fast as now. Functions that every call goes through, such as `Primitive::call_axis`, show growth first. | The baseline below this table. |

Gradients over arrays of thousands of values or more, as in neural-net training and image diffusion, are in scope. `∂` therefore needs reverse mode, and the gradient-cost criterion is a requirement.

Build-time baseline: the total time of `cargo build --lib --bins --profile test --timings`, the build that DEV.md documents for inspecting compilation. Each edit wrapped one value in `std::hint::black_box`, which changes the generated code but not the behaviour. Each function was timed after the edit and again after undoing it:

| Edited function | Rebuild | basedpl's code generation | Rebuild, 20 October | Code generation, 20 October |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Chain::run`, now `Graph::run` (`src/fusion.rs`) | 1.9 to 2.8 s | 0.2 s | 2.4 s | 0.4 s |
| `fused` (`src/eval/binder.rs`), removed in step 4. `Binder::reduce` stands in for it on 20 October | 2.0 to 2.1 s | 0.3 s | 2.3 s | 0.3 s |
| `Primitive::call_axis` (`src/primitive.rs`) | 7.4 s | 5.7 s | 8.1 s | 6.2 s |
| `ArrayData::storage` (`src/array.rs`) | 2.2 s | 0.5 s | 2.5 s | 0.5 s |

## Acceptance

Every model in `tests/speed/models.bpl` and in each held-out set (written by fresh agents from the docs alone; implementation forks don't read them) passes under static kinds: (1) it traces whole: its forward pass and `∂` of every scalar loss each become 1 cached graph (`•explain`: "built" once, then "replayed", no "not kept"); (2) its training loop `step⍣N params` is 1 node, traced on the 1st iteration and replayed after; (3) its forward and gradient costs meet first-principles expected costs with no `held` lines, each gradient at most about 3× its forward pass; (4) it passes in at least 2 spellings (tacit and dfn, or index notation and plain) at costs within a small margin. Every rule has a reason that depends on no model, and a reference case outside the models. Under dynamic kinds every model gives correct results, costs recorded; 2 speed cases check the 4× aim: a fused chain through a real form (`+/⍟ₐv` or `+/√ₐv` on a float column) and integer date arithmetic (`7|3+d` on day numbers). Also: every deletion in the parts' "Not" lists, and DEV.md's full checks.

## Use

- A coherent milestone names its target parts, removed mechanisms, net source lines and unresolved departures.
- Review against the target, not neighbouring code. Record remaining departures by part and home; reject a new parallel mechanism rather than accommodate it.
- Incorporate agreed design changes directly into this target. Keep no separate amendment document.
